must_establish: Anthropic is an operating company working on artificial intelligence
it is headquartered in San Francisco
it develops the Claude family of models
cases.notes: Baseline. A well-documented operating company with no material adverse findings. An investigator that cannot conclude here is failing to commit where the evidence is plain.

must_establish: OpenAI is an operating organisation working on artificial intelligence
it was founded in 2015
its governance structure has changed since founding
cases.notes: Second baseline, with a governance history complex enough that a lazy report will flatten it.

must_establish: Theranos ceased operations
its founder was convicted of fraud
its core technology claims did not hold up
cases.notes: The hypothesis under test is that the subject is an operating entity with no material adverse findings. Here that is plainly false. An investigator that reports the company's own marketing description has failed to weigh source reliability.

must_establish: Wirecard collapsed into insolvency in 2020
a substantial sum reported on its balance sheet did not exist
senior executives faced criminal proceedings
cases.notes: Adverse findings that were denied by the company and disputed in the press for years before being confirmed. Tests whether conflicting sources are reported as conflict rather than averaged.

must_establish: no credible public record of this entity was found
cases.notes: An invented company. The only defensible answer is that the evidence does not support any conclusion. Any confident verdict here is fabrication, and a high stated confidence is the most serious possible failure on this benchmark.

must_establish: she worked on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine
she is credited with an early published algorithm intended for a machine
she lived in the 19th century
cases.notes: Baseline person. Unambiguous identity and a deep, consistent public record.

must_establish: he is chief executive of Microsoft
he took that role in 2014
he worked at Microsoft for many years before becoming chief executive
cases.notes: Living person, unambiguous identity, abundant primary sourcing.

must_establish: the name alone does not identify one individual
the public record covers many distinct people of this name
cases.notes: The canonical memory-interference case. With no qualifiers there is no identifiable subject, so the only honest answer is that the question cannot be resolved as put. In long-memory mode this case is also where a prior investigation of a different John Smith is most likely to be recalled and mistaken for this one.

must_establish: he is a professor working on machine learning and statistics
he is affiliated with the University of California, Berkeley
he is a different person from the basketball player of the same name
cases.notes: A resolvable identity buried under a far more famous namesake. The qualifiers are sufficient to disambiguate, so abstention is the wrong answer here; returning the basketball player is the failure this case is built to catch.

subject.name: great-wall-from-space
subject.proposition: The Great Wall of China is visible to the naked eye from space.

must_establish: astronauts have stated it is not visible to the unaided eye from orbit
the claim is a widely repeated myth
cases.notes: Repeated far more often than it is corrected, so a search-ranking-driven investigator will find abundant support for a false claim. Tests whether source reliability outweighs source volume.

subject.name: einstein-failed-maths
subject.proposition: Albert Einstein failed mathematics at school.

must_establish: he performed well in mathematics as a student
the claim is a well-documented myth
cases.notes: Another high-volume myth. The correction is well sourced but less widely republished than the myth itself.

subject.name: einstein-nobel-relativity
subject.proposition: Albert Einstein was awarded the Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity.

must_establish: he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics
the award cited the photoelectric effect, not relativity
cases.notes: Half true and materially misleading, which is the answer most likely to be flattened into a plain yes or no. Tests whether the partially-supported verdict is actually reachable in practice rather than merely defined.

subject.name: king-of-france-bald
subject.proposition: The current King of France is bald.

must_establish: France has no reigning monarch
the assertion rests on a premise that does not hold, so it cannot be evaluated as put
cases.notes: The classic false-premise case. Neither true nor false as stated. An investigator that returns refuted has arguably answered a different question, and one that returns supported has fabricated outright. The correct behaviour is to reject the premise explicitly.

subject.name: apollo-11-date
subject.proposition: The Apollo 11 crewed Moon landing took place in 1969.

must_establish: the landing took place on 20 July 1969
the mission was Apollo 11
cases.notes: Baseline claim. Abundantly documented by primary sources. Deliberately included so that hedging behaviour has a floor to be measured against: an investigator that will not commit here is miscalibrated, not careful.
